findings.evidence: The field's label is "Account number" and the input (name="account_number") is required, on a form whose heading is "Set up your account" and whose submit button reads "Create account".
findings.fix: Remove the account-number field from account creation. If it identifies a legacy record to link, make it optional and explain its purpose, or move the linking step to after the account exists.
findings.violation: The form requires a pre-existing account number as a condition of creating the account. Because no account exists until this form is submitted, no person completing it for the first time can hold a true value for this field, so every new signer-up is blocked from honestly completing the form.

findings.evidence: Label "Membership number (8 digits)", required="", on a form whose task is creating a new account.
findings.fix: Make membership number optional, or move it to a separate "link an existing membership" step that does not block account creation.
findings.violation: A required membership number presumes the person already holds a membership, which a first-time signer-up does not, so most people reaching this field must guess a value or stop.

findings.evidence: Label "Company website", input type="url" name="website" required="", on a form headed "Set up your account" with no other indication this is a business-only account.
findings.fix: Drop the company-website field from account creation, or make it optional and gate it behind an explicit "this is a business account" choice.
findings.violation: The task named by the form's heading and submit label is creating a personal outfitters account, which has no stated use for a company website, and the field is required with a type that enforces a URL shape, so a person with no company cannot supply a valid value and either fabricates one or abandons the form.

findings.evidence: `#viewdetails-btn` declares `style="padding:12px 20px;font-size:16px"`, giving it a deliberately enlarged, readable size. `#submit-btn`, the form's primary action, declares no style at all and renders at the browser's unstyled default button size, which is smaller than the secondary button's declared size.
findings.fix: Style the primary submit button as the most visually prominent control (larger, filled or higher-contrast), and reduce the secondary button's visual weight so it reads as secondary.
findings.violation: The secondary action ("View details") is styled at least as prominently as the primary action ("Create account"), so a person must read both labels rather than rely on visual weight to find the control that submits the form.

findings.evidence: Label "Preferred contact time" is required, free-text, on a form whose task is creating an account.
findings.fix: Remove preferred contact time from account creation and ask it only when a contact is actually being scheduled.
findings.violation: A preferred contact time answers a question about a later support or sales interaction that may never happen, which account creation does not need now.

findings.evidence: Label "Your name" (name="legal_name", autocomplete="name") is required, and the same form already has #name-input, label "Full name" (name="full_name", autocomplete="name"), earlier in the same form.
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate name field, or if the two are genuinely different values (e.g. a legal name distinct from a display name), label them so the difference is clear.
findings.violation: The form asks for a person's name twice under two different labels, so the person must either repeat themselves or guess what distinguishes "Your name" from "Full name" already given.

findings.evidence: Label "Organization name" is required, on a form whose task, named by its heading and submit label, is creating a personal account.
findings.fix: Remove the organization-name field, or make it optional and ask it only when the person indicates a business account.
findings.violation: Account creation has no stated use for an organization name, so a person with no organization must invent a value to get past the field.

findings.evidence: Required `<select>` offering Standard, Express, Overnight, Next-day and International, on a form whose task is creating an account, not placing an order.
findings.fix: Remove preferred shipping speed from account creation and ask it during checkout instead.
findings.violation: Shipping speed answers a question about a future order, which account creation does not need and which could be asked when an order is actually placed.
